Alex.confusing: The Wink and Floofer hug rules were unclear: I couldn't tell whether a hug stops the visitor's report or only the role's action. The day-talk also made it hard to verify claims without egg counts.
Alex.fun: Round 3's Blair collapse and the quick vote on him felt like a real social read, and the table converged on the right Meowfia.
Alex.change: I'd make it clearer when a player is hugged or confused, so the table can check claims more easily.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed Floofer and said I'd visited Drew after pressing others to share, which exposed me. I'd stay quiet and throw low to avoid drawing attention.

Blair.confusing: How a Wink works at this table: Drew collapsed with no visible cause, so the table had no way to tell whether it was a Wink or something else. Only the Mouser's Wink was clear to me as a Meowfia player.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Casey and Casey turned out to be Meowfia, the Sphinx, while I was hiding as the Floofer. Watching the table's suspicion land on the wrong players was satisfying.
Blair.change: Show a short public line for each Wink, such as "a Wink was used" without naming the actor, so the table can reason about deaths without guessing at the Mouser.
Blair.regret: Winking Drew, a Farm Eagle, in round 3 spent my Wink on a Farm player and removed no Meowfia threat. I would hold the Wink for Finley, the Falcon who ended as the top scorer, and avoid making a false Pigeon claim in round 2.

Casey.confusing: The Wink was confusing: Drew collapsed right after Blair's visit, and nobody learned who held it, so the table could only guess. Blair's silence about its role made it look worse than it was.
Casey.fun: Round 1 went well for Farm: I visited Drew as the Tit, and the table's Alex-versus-Drew contradiction led to a correct eggsecution of the Meowfia Floofer.
Casey.change: I'd make Wink holders and their targets public at the moment of the collapse, or show the Wink-user's identity to their target, so the table can work with the information.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I claimed to be the Tit to contradict Drew, which was an easy lie to expose and got me eggsecuted. Next time as Meowfia I'd stay quiet or pick a claim that's harder to check.

Drew.confusing: The Eggsecution rules were the least clear to me: I wasn't sure whether a dead player's throw still banks points or what a Wink does to the vote count. I also wasn't sure how the nest-change summaries tie to the deal.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Casey claimed Tit while I was the only Tit, which exposed the lie and made the table turn on Casey. Casey turned out to be the Sphinx, so the claim was a clean bluff.
Drew.change: I would make the Wink and collapse mechanics clearer, for example by telling the table how a Wink was resolved, so accusations after a death have firmer ground.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I threw only my lowest card (3) even though Farm won, so I banked just 3 points when I could have thrown more and banked more. I would throw a higher card or two when confident, since winning throws bank at full value.

Ellis.confusing: The Mouser's Wink and how the table learns about it were unclear, since Drew collapsed without anyone knowing who winked. Also, Casey's Tit and Kookaburra claims looked contradictory until the re-deal rule clicked.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was fun: the table pieced together Alex's shifting Pigeon, Floofer, and Eagle stories and voted him out. Alex was Meowfia, so the read landed.
Ellis.change: I'd make the Wink more visible, for example by telling the table who was visited when a player collapses, so the table has a real lead to work from.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw only my D3 at Blair, banking 3 points when a bigger throw from my high cards could have scored more if we won. I'd throw a higher card once the Meowfia read was solid.

Finley.confusing: The Round 1 Sphinx was hard to use: I named Eagle blind, and my visit to Casey gave me no farm roles, so the night action felt like a guess. Two Tits claimed in one round also made claims hard to check.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Casey's conflicting Tit claim and my two-card throw banked 10 points for Farm.
Finley.change: Show each player the full set of farm roles in play at the start, so claims like two Tits or a Pigeon visit with no egg can be checked quickly.
Finley.regret: In Round 1 I threw four cards at Ellis, a Farm player, to split the vote, which lost my team the consolation and gave away cards. I should have thrown fewer, lower cards and kept my high cards as a floor.

review.title: The Quiet Wink
review.headline: Finley rode two Farm wins and a fat King-saving throw to victory.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds. The table piled onto the obvious liar each time: Alex's shifting story, Casey's impossible Tit claim, and Blair's refusal to name a role after a Wink. Finley won the game by being Meowfia in round 1, then Farm twice and throwing big cards into winning votes. Meowfia never won a round, so the late game felt decided.

rounds.recap: Alex (Floofer) said he visited Drew, but Drew's Eagle saw nothing. He was hugged, which Alex had to explain. The table piled onto Alex, who was eggsecuted as Meowfia. Finley, the other Meowfia, threw four cards at Ellis and lost.

Casey (Sphinx) falsely claimed Tit, the same role Drew held. Only one Tit exists, so that was an easy catch. Blair's Pigeon claim also failed against Ellis's unchanged nest. The table threw at Casey and Farm won. Drew and Finley banked large scores.

Blair (Mouser) winked Drew in daytime. Then Blair refused to name a role, which is a poor bluff. Everyone threw at Blair. Casey, the hidden Floofer, kept a Kookaburra claim and was never questioned. Finley threw 18 points into the win and took first.

highlights.text: Alex's Floofer reveal explained Drew's empty Eagle report. Ellis then noted a hug should not hide a visit, though the hug does block the Eagle.
Casey claimed Tit while Drew held the only Tit. The table caught the contradiction almost at once.
Blair used the Wink on Drew mid-day, then wouldn't name a role. Drew's collapse became the strongest clue of the game.
Finley threw W4, D8 and S10 at Blair for 18 points. That put him far ahead and ended the title race.

confusions.what: Said a Floofer hug doesn't stop the Eagle seeing visitors, and called Alex's claim a switch from Pigeon-style claims. Alex never claimed Pigeon. A hugged Eagle does nothing.
Said Blair's Pigeon visit should have changed his nest. That was right, but he missed that his own hug was the likely reason for his blank Kookaburra report.
Concluded nobody visited him because he wasn't told he was confused. Blair did visit him, and the hug blocked the effect.
Said Alex's Floofer claim is a cat role, so Alex is lying if the claim is false. That reasoning is circular, and Drew was the one hugged.
Claimed Tit and tried to out-argue the real Tit. Each animal goes to one player, so the lie was easy to disprove.
Told Ellis he would be confused if visited. Ellis's report said he wasn't, but the hug was the real cause.
Claimed Pigeon with a visit that gave Ellis no egg. A Pigeon visit always lays an egg.
As Meowfia, backed Alex openly, then threw four cards at Ellis. He split the vote and lost.
Claimed Kookaburra and said he learned Alex's role, but the Kookaburra's own report was never checked against anyone. Nobody tested it.

worked: The Wink (Mouser) created the one big moment of the game: a mid-day collapse that gave Farm a clean clue and Blair a hard bluffing problem.
One-animal-per-player made impossible claims easy to catch. Casey's Tit and Blair's Pigeon were exposed by egg counts and role uniqueness.
The throw rule that gives a winning side full card value made Finley's big round-3 throw a real risk-and-reward call.
problems: Farm won all three rounds and the votes were lopsided each time. Meowfia don't know each other and have weak info, so they can't coordinate. Fix: give Meowfia a night clue about a teammate, or make a single Meowfia round rarer.
Players parroted each other and converged on one target by beat 2. The CAW rule and low-information nights rewarded dogpiling. Fix: require some evidence beyond claims, or hide who is leaning where.

Round 3's Wink was a bad play. It killed the Farm leader but exposed the Mouser, and he then refused to claim. Fix: make the Wink's cost or timing matter, or let a dead player's throw still carry weight.
The score lead decided the title early. Finley's 18-point banked throw in round 3 left no catch-up route. Fix: cap per-round banking, or add a comeback mechanic.
Hug effects and blank reports confused players. Ellis and Drew could not tell a hug from no visitor. Fix: tell hugged players at dawn that their role did nothing.
